Stated Claim / Post Context:
Pediatrician complained of feeling 'drugged' in weeks before husband allegedly murdered her and set body on fire while couple's young daughter slept nearby, investigators say

Dr Julia Pederson, 41, was found dead around 7.05am on October 10 in Harrisburg after a fire broke out at the couple's home. Her death was ruled a homicide.

Actual Article Body:
By ALYSSA GUZMAN, US NEWS REPORTER

Published:  01:15 AEDT, 23 October 2026   |  Updated:  02:12 AEDT, 23 October 2026

A Pennsylvania pediatrician had reportedly claimed she felt 'drugged' in the weeks leading up to her murder, investigators said.

Dr Julia Pederson, 41, was found dead around 7.05am on October 10 in Harrisburg after a fire broke out at the couple's home.

A medical examiner later ruled her death a homicide and said she died before the fire.

Her estranged husband, Jonathan Gatto, 42, has been accused of strangling his wife. He was arrested and charged with first-degree murder, abuse of a corpse, and more.

Now, a search warrant, obtained by PennLive, revealed Pederson had told relatives that she felt 'drugged' in the days leading up to her death.

In a September 10 message, Pederson told her mother that she could barely walk and was feeling groggy and feared she had been drugged. She also told her mother she had to cancel five patients' appointments as she was so unwell.

One of Pederson's colleagues told investigators on Friday that Gatto and the couple's seven-year-old daughter dropped off drinks to the pediatrician daily, despite the mother not wanting them, the warrant said.

Her colleague reported that Pederson would become lethargic, start having migraine symptoms, and would get dizzy after consuming the beverages.

Dr Julia Pederson, 41, was found dead around 7.05am on October 10. In the weeks leading up to her death, she told relatives she felted drugged

Her estranged husband, Jonathan Gatto, was arrested on October 13 on first-degree murder charges, among others

On October 9, the doctor had to lie down on her office floor, the warrant said. She had scheduled bloodwork for the next day, but never made the appointment as she was found dead.

Investigators requested DNA samples from all family members. They also requested to collect 'any and all water bottles, water containers, and food containers that may have been used' by the doctor, the warrant said.

Investigators also requested to search for any 'flammable liquid containers and/or flammable chemicals,' security camera footage, and paperwork regarding the couple's relationship.

On October 13, Gatto was arrested. He was denied bail due to the severity of the charges and is being held at the Dauphin County Prison.

On the same day, an autopsy found that Pederson died from multiple traumatic injuries.

Two days later, the district attorney and the Harrisburg Police Department were seen at the home, including an officer wearing a Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) vest.

The ATF is a federal agency that investigates arson cases.

Investigators were seen carrying out cardboard boxes and paper bags, according to PennLive. They were at the home for a little over an hour.

A medical examiner ruled Pederson died before the fire was set in their home and ruled her death a homicide

Gatto told police during an interview that the couple intended to get a separation because of marriage struggles and were deciding how to tell their daughter, according to an affidavit seen by WGAL.

Gatto claimed he suddenly woke up to smoke detectors going off, causing him to rush into the home's downstairs bedroom to get the little girl.

He told police he returned for Pederson, but burned his hand trying to get into the room, per the affidavit. Blood tests showed Pederson had been dead before the fire started.

Gatto allegedly told law enforcement that Pederson had not been feeling well on October 9 after starting to take new medication for her migraines.

He claimed to have heard a loud sound around 11pm or midnight that resembled someone falling down the stairs, according to the affidavit.

Gatto said he asked Pederson if she was okay, to which she allegedly mumbled and closed the bedroom door, WHP reported.

Law enforcement also allegedly heard that Gatto returned to the bedroom around 2am to bring his wife ibuprofen.

However, Pederson was allegedly startled, and he went back to bed, legal documents said.

A coworker told investigators that Pederson would fall ill after drinking the daily beverages her daughter and Gatto dropped off for her

When Gatto woke up again to the smoke detectors later, he claimed that he was effectively unable to reach Pederson because of the blaze inside the bedroom.

He then waited for emergency crews outside, per the legal document.

The blaze was described as 'very small' by investigators, while a Pennsylvania State Police fire marshal found that it had been intentionally set after inspecting the scene.

Firefighters observed light smoke coming from the home, according to the affidavit.

First responders performed CPR on Pederson and then rushed her to the Penn State Health Holy Spirit Medical Center, where she was declared dead.

Pederson was a Harvard University graduate who received her medical degree from Stanford's School of Medicine and did her pediatric residency at Lurie Children's Hospital in Chicago.

The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) told CBS 21 that it was 'deeply saddened' by Pederson's death.

UPMC called Pederson a 'beloved pediatrician' and a 'valued member' of its Children's Community Pediatrics team.

Pederson had a blood test scheduled for the day she was found dead

'Dr Pederson devoted her career to caring for children and supporting families, and her loss is felt deeply by colleagues, patients, and communities she served,' the statement continued.

Pederson joined the hospital in February, according to UPMC.

The Daily Mail has reached out to Gatto's lawyers for comment.
